items.title: Iran war, crude, rupee among 8 factors to steer D-Street in holiday-shortened week
items.description: The Indian stock market faces a holiday-shortened week with significant headwinds. Geopolitical tensions from the Iran-Israel conflict, elevated crude oil prices, and a depreciating rupee are expected to weigh on investor sentiment. Foreign institutional investors continue their selling spree, adding to market uncertainties.

items.title: Stock market open for only 3 days this week. Anand James on how to trade Nifty
items.description: Indian stock markets will trade for only three days this week. This shortened trading period, combined with settlement holidays, is expected to increase market volatility. Investors should be aware of potential deferred reactions to global events. Nifty IT shows resilience, while PSU banks are in a corrective phase.

items.title: Macro shock, macro strength: 9 stocks from different sectors but with one common factor, and upside potential of up to 32%
items.description: When any conflict in the Gulf region escalates, the market usually reacts first and asks questions later. At this juncture, when every stock has suffered another round of decline, investors are probably thinking about what will happen to their portfolios in light of the ongoing war. That instinct is both natural and understandable. But remember: This war will end and the market will get back to doing what it normally does – reward companies with growth and earnings.
